value: How far below the bottom of a trench support system's members may material be excavated, and on what conditions?
reason: 1926.652(e)(2)(i), p. 343, sets two conditions, not one: design for full-depth forces 'and there are no indications while the trench is open of a possible loss of soil from behind or below the bottom of the support system'.

value: Up to 2 feet, if designed for the trench's full-depth forces, with no sign of soil loss from behind or below the system.
reason: The back gave only the design condition as if it were the whole rule; 1926.652(e)(2)(i), p. 343, also requires no indications of soil loss from behind or below the support system while the trench is open.

value: Both conditions apply: the design must cover the forces of the trench's full depth, and while the trench is open there must be no sign of soil being lost from behind or below the support system.
reason: Explanation now covers both conditions of 1926.652(e)(2)(i), p. 343.

value: 2 feet (.61 m) below the bottom of the members of a support system shall be permitted, but only if the system is designed to resist the forces calculated for the full depth of the trench, and there are no indications while the trench is open of a possible loss of soil from behind or below

value: A positive "on-off" control on its own is permitted.

value: An exposure averaged over an 8-hour workday; under the lead standard, short exposures above the limit are allowed if the day's average stays within it.
reason: The front asks what a TWA is in general, but the second half comes from the lead appendix (1926.62 App. B, p. 98). It is not true of every TWA limit: asbestos also has a 30-minute excursion limit of 1.0 f/cc (1926.1101(c)(2), p. 531), which caps short peaks.

reason: The 12-month practice duty is in 1926.1211(b)(4), which covers an employer whose own employees are designated to provide rescue (p. 667–668: '(b) An employer whose employees have been designated to provide permit space rescue and/or emergency services must...'). The old front did not say whose practice it was.

value: 29 CFR 1926.1211(b)(4), Rescue and emergency services, p. 668
reason: The source line named no paragraph; the practice duty is 1926.1211(b)(4).

value: The attendant stays outside and summons rescue and emergency services. Only a relieved attendant who is trained and equipped for rescue, under a programme that allows it, may go in.
reason: The key tells the attendant only what not to do. 1926.1209(g), p. 666, gives the positive duty: 'Summons rescue and other emergency services as soon as the attendant determines that authorized entrants may need assistance to escape from permit space hazards'.
